title: OET Reading Part B Practice
note: Unofficial self-study. Short workplace extracts · 3 options.

sets.title: Ward extracts — set 1
sets.instruction: Read each extract and choose the answer that fits best.

items.extract:
From a hospital policy on medication reconciliation:

Medicines reconciliation must be completed within 24 hours of admission. Discrepancies between the patient’s reported list and the electronic record should be clarified with the usual GP or community pharmacy before discharge prescribing is finalised.
items.stem: The policy mainly requires staff to

options.text: ignore community pharmacy information.
reconcile medicines early and resolve list discrepancies before final discharge prescriptions.
delay all prescribing until after discharge.

items.explain: Complete reconciliation within 24h and clarify discrepancies before finalising discharge prescribing.

items.extract:
Email from the endoscopy lead:

Please stop sending ‘urgent’ booking requests without stating the indication and anticoagulation status. Incomplete forms are returned, which delays the patients you are trying to prioritise.
items.stem: The lead’s main concern is that

options.text: urgent requests are never appropriate.
missing clinical details cause returns and delay care.
anticoagulation is irrelevant to endoscopy.

items.explain: Incomplete forms are returned and delay the patients being prioritised.

items.extract:
Nursing handover note:

Mrs Lee’s NEWS2 has risen from 3 to 6 since midday, mainly due to respiratory rate and new confusion. Medical review requested; oxygen started per protocol. Family updated.

options.text: observations are stable and no review is needed.
deterioration has prompted protocol oxygen and a medical review request.
confusion alone explains the score without breathing change.

items.explain: NEWS2 rise with RR and confusion; oxygen per protocol; medical review requested.

items.extract:
Pharmacy bulletin:

Do not crush modified-release metformin tablets. If a patient cannot swallow solids, contact pharmacy for an appropriate alternative rather than altering the solid dose form.

options.text: crush modified-release metformin when swallowing is difficult.
ask pharmacy for an alternative instead of crushing modified-release tablets.
stop metformin permanently in all dysphagic patients.

items.explain: Do not crush MR metformin; contact pharmacy for an alternative.

items.extract:
Occupational health memo:

Staff with unprotected exposure to measles should contact OH the same day, even if immunisation history seems complete. Exclusion advice depends on immunity evidence, not job title.

options.text: only unvaccinated cleaners need to call OH.
same-day contact is expected after unprotected measles exposure; exclusion follows immunity evidence.
job title determines exclusion more than immunity.

items.explain: Contact OH same day; exclusion depends on immunity evidence, not job title.

items.extract:
Discharge checklist reminder:

Confirm follow-up appointments are booked before the patient leaves the ward. ‘To be arranged by GP’ is acceptable only when the receiving practice has already acknowledged the request in writing.

options.text: all follow-up may be left vaguely to the GP without acknowledgement.
booked follow-up should be confirmed before discharge, with written acknowledgement if GP arrangement is used.
wards should never involve GPs in follow-up.

items.explain: Confirm bookings before leaving; GP arrangement only with written acknowledgement.

gist: Part B = purpose of the extract, not trivia.
Underline the policy verb: must / do not / contact / confirm.

vocab.gloss: 대사·대조: 약 목록을 맞춰 확인하는 것

sets.title: Clinic & theatre extracts — set 2
sets.instruction: Choose the option that best matches the extract.

items.extract:
Pre-op assessment guidance:

Patients on SGLT2 inhibitors should usually omit the dose on the day of surgery and, for longer fasting or high-risk procedures, the day before as well — confirm with the anaesthetist if unsure.
items.stem: The guidance mainly tells staff to

options.text: continue SGLT2 inhibitors without change.
omit peri-operative doses as described and check with anaesthesia when uncertain.
stop all diabetes medicines permanently before any operation.

items.explain: Omit day-of (and sometimes day-before) doses; confirm with anaesthetist if unsure.

items.extract:
Infection control update:

Visors alone are not a substitute for a fluid-resistant surgical mask during aerosol-generating procedures. Both mask and eye protection are required unless a higher-specification respirator is indicated.

options.text: visors replace masks for aerosol-generating procedures.
mask plus eye protection are required; visors alone are not enough.
eye protection is optional if a visor is worn.

items.explain: Visors alone are not a substitute; both mask and eye protection required.

items.extract:
Outpatient letter standard:

Copy patients into clinic letters unless they opt out. Avoid unexplained abbreviations that a non-specialist reader would not understand.

options.text: never send letters to patients.
include patients by default and write in accessible language.
use as many abbreviations as possible to save space.

items.explain: Copy patients unless opt out; avoid unexplained abbreviations.

items.extract:
Blood transfusion checklist:

Two trained staff must check identity at the bedside immediately before transfusion begins. Checking in a corridor or treatment room without the patient present is not acceptable.
items.stem: The checklist emphasises that identity checks must be

options.text: done away from the patient to reduce anxiety.
completed by two trained staff at the bedside just before starting.
performed by one person if the ward is busy.

items.explain: Two trained staff at bedside immediately before transfusion; not elsewhere without patient.

items.extract:
Falls prevention brief:

A completed falls risk score does not replace continuous clinical observation. If a patient becomes newly restless or attempts to climb out of bed, escalate promptly even if the morning score was low.

options.text: a low morning score guarantees safety all day.
changing behaviour still needs escalation despite an earlier low score.
risk scores should never be used.

items.explain: Score does not replace observation; escalate new restlessness even if morning score low.

items.extract:
Research governance note:

Staff may discuss a study with eligible patients but must not obtain consent unless they are on the delegation log and have completed required training.
items.stem: According to the note, consent may be taken only by staff who

options.text: have casually heard about the trial.
are delegated and trained for that duty.
work on any ward in the hospital.

items.explain: Consent only if on delegation log and training completed.

gist: Find the rule and the exception; ignore tempting absolute options.

vocab.gloss: 위임 기록: 누가 무엇을 해도 되는지 적은 목록
